gpt-5-mini.exact_reserve_text:
The 2012 year of account ran off on a satisfactory basis as longstanding reserves continued their trend of steady release as remaining open items were either identified as redundant or finally settled as a result of negotiation or litigation. The result led to residual net reserves at year end totalling less than GBP 3.5m. That steady improvement was reflected by a calendar year profit of GBP 2.4m which contributed to the overall closing profit after three years of GBP 17.4m, as the 2012 year was finally closed into the 2014 year.

The 2014 year of account experienced different fortunes. The calendar year loss of GBP 5.6m arose primarily from the need to strengthen reserves for a small number of major items in litigation, as well as a need to adjust various reinsurance balances. Although the most material strengthening related to the CCI book where liabilities remain the subject of ongoing legal dispute, there was also need to increase specific reserves for a small number of disputed items in the UK, Italy and the USA all of which were the subjects of adverse legal developments. As a result of that strengthening, net reserves at year end totalled GBP 17.0m. It is hoped and expected that the most significant matters still in dispute will see final resolution during the first half of 2015, which will remove the most material sources of uncertainty governing final outcome.

prior_year_events.impact_description: Longstanding reserves on the 2012 year continued a trend of steady release as remaining open items were identified as redundant or settled, producing residual net reserves of less than GBP 3.5m and contributing to the three-year closing profit.
Adverse legal developments in the Contingent Cost Insurance (CCI) book required material strengthening of reserves.

gpt-5-mini.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims reserves at 1 January 2014 were GBP 7.578m. The syndicate experienced mixed reserve development during 2014: older years (notably the 2012 year) continued to show steady releases as long-standing items were settled, while the 2014 year required reserve strengthening primarily due to adverse legal developments (notably in the CCI book) and adjustments to reinsurance balances. No explicit gross prior-year development figure is quoted in the financial statements; the report describes net releases on closed years and net strengthenings on 2014 driven by litigation and reinsurance adjustments.
